# RCA: SAHME-3448
Summary: Request to trigger a refund on the cancelled order.
Generated: 2026-09-28T14:30:00Z

Issue:
Order ZA260822-65631545 was cancelled but the refund of R8,999.10 was never triggered. The payment was successfully captured on 2026-08-24 at 09:11:20, the order was moved to CANCELLED status with fullyCancelled=true, and the cancel-related email notifications were sent. However, no refund payment transaction entry was ever created. The order process (order-process-v25-69) and consignment process (consignment-process-v11-36) are both stuck in RUNNING state, and the consignment remains in WAITING_FOR_TRANSFER_CANCELLING.

RCA:
The order was created on 2026-08-24 at 09:00:51 with a total value of R8,999.10 (subtotal R10,999.00 + tax R1,173.80) using the za-floatPaymentMode. Payment was authorized and captured successfully at 09:11:20. The order was subsequently cancelled and moved to CANCELLED status with fullyCancelled=true. All price fields were zeroed out as expected after cancellation.

Three email processes completed successfully: sendOrderAcknowledgementEmailProcess, sendOrderCancelRequestEmailProcess, and sendOrderCancelledEmailProcess. However, the main order process (order-process-v25-69) is still in RUNNING state with its last executed action being isCancelledBeforeFinancialUpdateV1. This action evaluates whether the order was cancelled before the financial update was sent. Since fiPosted=false and the order is CANCELLED, this condition should evaluate to true and route the process to the refund path (refundCancelOrder). The process has not progressed past this decision point.

The consignment (ZA260822-65631545) is in WAITING_FOR_TRANSFER_CANCELLING status with warehouse WC11, and its consignment process (consignment-process-v11-36) is also stuck in RUNNING. The cancelRequestSentToLogistics flag is false, meaning the cancel request was never sent to the logistics system. The order process is likely blocked waiting for the consignment cancellation to complete before it can proceed to the refund step. Since the consignment cancellation never finalized, the order process never reached refundCancelOrder, and no refund payment transaction entry was created.

No return requests exist for this order, and no external service entries were found. There are no BusinessProcessParameter error entries (no stack traces stored) since the process is in RUNNING, not ERROR state.

This is the same pattern observed in SAHME-3376 (order ZA260521-83842685, same reporter Lerato) where a ZA-region order was cancelled before DO creation but the refund did not trigger. In that case, the payment team processed a manual refund because the order process had already completed without triggering the refund.

Possible remediation:
Two approaches are available:

Approach 1 — Process restart: Restart the order process from the refundCancelOrder action using the refund retrigger script (adapted from script-SAME-3941-refund-retrigger.groovy under PC-52765). The script needs to be modified to recognize isCancelledBeforeFinancialUpdateV1 as a valid restart point and use forceRetrigger=true since the process is in RUNNING state, not ERROR. This would attempt to re-trigger the automated refund flow.

Approach 2 — Manual refund: If the automated process restart does not succeed (as was the case with SAHME-3376), the payment team can process a manual refund of R8,999.10 to the customer. The capture transaction (ZA260822-65631545_8b5ca128-52c7-4684-bc86-54832dbd29c8, CAPTURE, ACCEPTED, R8,999.10) provides the reference for the manual refund.

Kibana logs were not available during this investigation (cookie bridge rate-limited). The DB state is conclusive, but log analysis would provide additional confirmation of the exact blocking condition at isCancelledBeforeFinancialUpdateV1.

Expert Care Orders Stuck || 29-Sep
Generated: 2026-10-02T18:00:00+09:00

Issue:
6 UAE Expert Care (GCIC) orders were reported stuck at SHIPPED status on 29-Sep. The orders are Galaxy Expert Care standalone service orders with GCIC_EXPERT_CARE_STANDALONE external service integration. DB verification on 2-Oct shows that 5 of the 6 orders have already been remediated and are now COMPLETED. One order (AE260922-91467505) remains stuck at SHIPPING_REQUESTED with a fundamentally different root cause from the other 5.

RCA:
Two distinct issues affected these orders:

Group 1 — 5 orders already remediated (AE260917-86564020, AE260917-86564071, AE260922-91048112, AE260922-91000993, AE260928-97214836):
All 5 had ExternalService (GCIC_EXPERT_CARE_STANDALONE) in ERROR status because the GCIC API call failed during order processing. The ExternalService ERROR state blocked the order process from completing, leaving consignments stuck at SHIPPED and the order process in ERROR state. These were remediated by PC-54773, which reset the ExternalService from ERROR to NEW and restarted the order process from processExternalServicesAction. All 5 are now COMPLETED with ExternalService status UPDATED and processes SUCCEEDED. Delivery mode for all 5 was ae-galaxy-expertCare-CarryIn, payment mode was ae-CheckoutDotComFlowPaymentMode.

Group 2 — 1 order still stuck (AE260922-91467505):
This order is fundamentally different. Key differences from Group 1:
- Order status is SHIPPING_REQUESTED (not SHIPPED) — the order never reached SHIPPED
- Consignment status is SHIPPING_REQUESTED with no shipped or completed dates, no GERP billing
- ExternalService (GCIC_EXPERT_CARE_STANDALONE) is in NEW status — the GCIC API was never called, the service was never attempted (not ERROR)
- Order process (order-process-v25-69) is in RUNNING state (not ERROR) — the process is alive but waiting
- Consignment process (consignment-process-v11-36) is also RUNNING
- Delivery mode is ae-galaxy-expertCare (without CarryIn) — a different fulfillment path from the other 5
- Payment mode is ae-tamaraPayment (Tamara BNPL) — different from the other 5 which used Checkout.com
- Process last action is isDelayedFiRequired — the process is stalled waiting for delayed financial integration

The order completed checkout and payment capture successfully (Tamara authorization and capture both ACCEPTED for 804 AED + 120 AED = 924 AED). However, the order process is stuck at the isDelayedFiRequired action. The ExternalService was created (status NEW) but the GCIC API call was never triggered because the process never reached the point where the external service would be activated for this delivery mode and payment flow. The Tamara BNPL payment path and the ae-galaxy-expertCare delivery mode (non-CarryIn) route through a different process branch that requires delayed FI posting before the consignment can progress. The delayed FI event from GERP was never received, causing the process to stall at isDelayedFiRequired. As a result, the consignment remains at SHIPPING_REQUESTED and the GCIC service activation was never initiated.

Similar tickets: AEME-5925 (Order Stuck | Expert Cleaning Orders) and AEME-6272 (Orders stuck at processExternalServices [GCIC_EXPERT_CLEANING_STANDALONE]) dealt with the same GCIC ExternalService ERROR pattern as Group 1. AE260922-91467505 does not match this pattern.

Possible remediation:
For the 5 already remediated orders: No action needed. All 5 are COMPLETED with processes SUCCEEDED. PC-54773 script was executed successfully.

For AE260922-91467505:
The remediation approach differs from the other 5 because the ExternalService is NEW (not ERROR) and the process is RUNNING (not ERROR). The following steps are recommended:

1. Set the consignment status from SHIPPING_REQUESTED to COMPLETED to simulate the service completion. This order is a standalone Expert Care service (ae-galaxy-expertCare) — there is no physical shipment, so the consignment completion represents the service being rendered.

2. Trigger the GCIC ExternalService by updating its status to trigger the GCIC API call, or manually setting the ExternalService to UPDATED if the service was already fulfilled out-of-band.

3. Restart the order process from the isDelayedFiRequired action to push it past the stalled FI wait, or alternatively restart from processExternalServicesAction to re-attempt the GCIC integration after setting the consignment to COMPLETED.

4. Verify the order progresses to COMPLETED and the order process reaches SUCCEEDED state.

PC-54773 is reusable for this ticket but the existing script only covers the 5 already-remediated orders. A new script or modification is needed for AE260922-91467505 with the different remediation approach (consignment status change + process restart from a different action). Alternatively, PC-46538 (TKME-2056: Orders stuck at processExternalServices [GCIC_EXPERT_CLEANING_STANDALONE]) may provide a reusable pattern for the consignment completion approach.

The existing PC-54773 script (script-AEME-6596-expert-care-remediation.groovy) is in the bin directory and can be adapted. The script should be updated to include AE260922-91467505 with the modified logic: set consignment to COMPLETED, optionally trigger GCIC, and restart the order process from the appropriate action.

solution.excerpt:
[PROD] | Manual Chargeback | 30th Sept
Generated: 2026-09-30T09:11:22Z

Issue:

Two distinct issues are reported in this ticket.

Part 1 - Manual Chargeback for Trade-In Rejected Orders:
Orders AE260814-59413370 (chargeback amount 270 AED) and AE260803-49001795 (chargeback amount 3035 AED) have completed delivery, but their trade-in devices were rejected by Northladder (ExternalService status = CANCELLED). The automated clawback/chargeback process should debit the trade-in discount amount back from the customer's card approximately 19 days after consignment completion. The automated clawback was attempted but failed, requiring manual intervention to retrigger.

Part 2 - Order Stuck at CHECKED_INVALID:
Order AE260928-97453028 (created 28th Sept, total 186.01 AED, Checkout.com payment) is stuck at CHECKED_INVALID status. No consignments were created, order processes are in FAILED state looping at the checkOrder action (50+ retries), and the order cannot progress to fulfilment.

RCA:

Part 1 - Chargeback Failure (AE260814-59413370, AE260803-49001795):

Both orders are COMPLETED with consignments delivered and GERP billing completed. The NORTHLADDER trade-in ExternalService is CANCELLED on both, confirming trade-in rejection. The field isChargeBackRefundDone is false (0) on both orders, and paymentStatus is NULL.

DB evidence shows a second PaymentTransaction on each order with an AUTHORIZATION entry in ERROR state:
- AE260814-59413370: AUTHORIZATION ERROR at 2026-09-18 02:01:46 (consignment completed 2026-08-29, ~19 day clawback trigger aligns)
- AE260803-49001795: AUTHORIZATION ERROR at 2026-09-13 02:01:52 (consignment completed 2026-08-20, ~19 day clawback trigger aligns)

This matches the pattern documented in the prior chargeback ticket AEME-6540 (closed, PC-53902). The RCA from that ticket states: "Clawback PaymentTransaction records lacked paymentInfo and requestId, causing the automated re-authorization to fail and requiring manual chargeback." The clawback process creates a new PaymentTransaction to perform an unscheduled MIT (Merchant Initiated Transaction) payment using the saved card credentials. When the paymentInfo or requestId is missing on the clawback PaymentTransaction, the re-authorization call to Checkout.com fails with PROCESSOR_DECLINE, and the clawback BusinessProcess enters ERROR state.

Root cause: The clawback PaymentTransaction for both orders lacks the required paymentInfo reference and requestId needed for the unscheduled MIT re-authorization. The automated clawback attempted after the 19-day window, but Checkout.com declined the payment because the card tokenization data was incomplete on the clawback PaymentTransaction. This is the same platform issue seen in AEME-6540, AEME-6362, and AEME-6286.

Part 2 - CHECKED_INVALID (AE260928-97453028):

The order was created on 2026-09-28 at 10:20:28 with payment mode ae-CheckoutDotComFlowPaymentMode. Two PaymentTransactions exist with AUTHORIZATION ACCEPTED entries (64.00 AED and 186.01 AED), confirming payment was authorized successfully. However, the order status is CHECKED_INVALID, zero consignments exist, and both order-process-v25-69 instances are in FAILED state.

Task logs show the checkOrder action executing 50+ times, indicating the order validation at the checkOrder action node is repeatedly failing. The order has an ExternalService for GCIC_EXPERT_CARE_STANDALONE in NEW status, suggesting the order contains a standalone service product that may be contributing to the validation failure.

The paymentStatus field is NULL on this order, and deliveryMode is also NULL, which are required fields for order validation. The checkOrder action in the order-process-v25-69 workflow validates order integrity (payment info, delivery mode, consignment creation prerequisites) before allowing the order to proceed to fulfilment. When this validation fails, the order is set to CHECKED_INVALID and the process enters FAILED state.

Root cause: The order failed validation at the checkOrder action node during the order-process-v25-69 workflow. The missing paymentStatus and deliveryMode fields, combined with the standalone Expert Care service (GCIC_EXPERT_CARE_STANDALONE) in NEW state, likely caused the checkOrder validation to reject the order and mark it CHECKED_INVALID. The process then entered a retry loop at checkOrder but cannot self-remediate because the underlying field gaps persist.

Possible remediation:

Part 1 - Chargeback Retrigger:

Reuse the existing approved script from AEME-6540 (PC-53902): script-AEME-6540-clawback-retrigger.groovy. This script:
1. Finds the clawback BusinessProcess for each order (WHERE code LIKE '%{orderCode}%Clawback%')
2. Sets the ERROR state process to CREATED (Hybris restartProcess fails on ERROR state)
3. Calls businessProcessService.restartProcess(bp, "reAuthorizeIfNeeded") to retrigger the clawback authorization

The script needs to be copied and updated with the new order codes (AE260814-59413370, AE260803-49001795) and the new ticket reference (AEME-6602). If the clawback fails again with PROCESSOR_DECLINE (as happened in AEME-6540), the paymentInfo and requestId on the clawback PaymentTransaction may need to be populated from the original order's PaymentTransaction before retriggering.

Note: The chargeback amounts (270 AED and 3035 AED) specified in the ticket should be verified against the trade-in discount amounts on the orders to ensure the clawback charges the correct amount.

Part 2 - CHECKED_INVALID Remediation:

Reuse the existing pattern from AEME-6548 (PC-52605): script-AEME-6548-order1-checked-invalid-retrigger.groovy. This script:
1. Sets order status from CHECKED_INVALID to CREATED
2. Restarts the FAILED order-process-v25-69 processes from the checkOrder action (last failed action)
3. Clears current tasks and forces process state to ERROR before restartProcess

Before running this, verify:
- That paymentStatus can be set (it is currently NULL — may need to set to PAID since AUTHORIZATION was ACCEPTED)
- That deliveryMode is available for this order's delivery address and can be set
- That the GCIC_EXPERT_CARE_STANDALONE external service in NEW status is not blocking order progression

If the checkOrder action fails again after restart (because the underlying field gaps are not fixed), a deeper investigation into the specific validation failure at checkOrder is needed. Kibana logs for AE260928-97453028 would reveal the exact exception message from the checkOrder action, but Kibana MCP was unavailable during this investigation.

References:
- AEME-6540 (Closed): Previous manual chargeback ticket with same root cause. Script: script-AEME-6540-clawback-retrigger.groovy (PC-53902)
- AEME-6362 (Closed): First manual chargeback ticket. Documented that the 19-day chargeback trigger cannot be overridden.
- AEME-6286 (Closed): Trade-in re-trigger chargeback ticket.
- AEME-6548 (Closed): CHECKED_INVALID remediation. Script: script-AEME-6548-order1-checked-invalid-retrigger.groovy (PC-52605 pattern)
- PC-53902: Approved PC ticket for clawback retrigger (AEME-6540)
- PC-52605: Approved PC ticket for CHECKED_INVALID retrigger (AEME-6548 pattern)

Limitations:
- Kibana MCP was unavailable during this investigation. Log analysis could not be performed. Root cause for Part 2 (CHECKED_INVALID) is based on DB state analysis and code pattern correlation only.
- Clawback BusinessProcess could not be queried directly via HAC (timeout). The clawback process existence is inferred from the ERROR-state PaymentTransactionEntry on both chargeback orders.

Ticket Summary: Stuck order on Hybris - ORDER_SPLIT
Generated: 2026-10-08T00:00:00Z

Issue:

6 TR-region orders reported stuck in ORDER_SPLIT status on 2026-09-25. All orders are buyback orders containing OmniChannelProduct, assigned to DIVA-Istanbul warehouse. Upon DB verification, 4 of the 6 orders have already self-resolved to COMPLETED status. One order (TR260925-94453037) remains genuinely stuck in ORDER_SPLIT, waiting for DIVA shipment status. One order (TR260925-94514044) progressed to REFUND_FAILED after its consignments were cancelled but the MasterPass refund of 450,000 TRY failed with ERROR status.

RCA:

TR260925-94249237, TR260925-94292417, TR260925-94546058, TR260925-94640512:
These 4 orders have fully completed. All consignments are COMPLETED, GERP billing numbers assigned, all order and consignment processes SUCCEEDED. No action needed — these progressed after the ticket was raised, likely as DIVA sent shipment confirmations.

TR260925-94453037 (ORDER_SPLIT — genuinely stuck):
The order was split into 3 consignments (products: AR60F24C1KW/SK, ACL-RF50, FRH1458Z4) after checkout via the splitOrder action in order-process-v25-69. All 3 consignments are assigned to DIVA-Istanbul warehouse and are in READY status. The order process reached the isDelayedFiRequired action node, which checks IsDelayedFiPostingRequiredAction.executeAction() — this calls RentalPaymentUtil.isRentalPaymentMode() on the order's payment mode. Since the payment mode is MasterPass (tr-masterpassPaymentMode, not a rental payment mode), the action returns NO, transitioning to waitForWarehouseSubprocessEnd. The order process is now waiting for the event ${process.code}_ConsignmentSubprocessEnd.

The 3 consignment subprocesses (omnichannel-consignment-sub-process-v1) are all in RUNNING state. These subprocesses are waiting for DIVA to send the shipment status for each consignment. DIVA has not yet sent the shipment confirmation for this order, so the consignment processes remain RUNNING, which means the ConsignmentSubprocessEnd event is never fired, and the order process stays stuck at waitForWarehouseSubprocessEnd.

This matches the pattern seen in TKME-2028 (15 TR-region orders stuck at ORDER_SPLIT, resolved after confirming with DIVA and manually updating status) and RT-349680 (DIVA orders stuck at Order Split, fixed by DIVA 3rd party). The Jira comment from Rajeshbabu Yatirajula confirms: "Only one order is still pending with DIVA, it will be moved further when hybris receives the shipment status from DIVA system."

TR260925-94514044 (REFUND_FAILED — partially stuck):
Both consignments were CANCELLED (one at WC12-S751, one at DIVA-Istanbul). The order was cancelled and a REFUND_FOLLOW_ON transaction for 450,000 TRY was initiated on 2026-10-05 11:30:31, but it failed with ERROR status. The order process (order-process-v25-69) is in RUNNING state, waiting at the financial completion path — the process expects the refund to complete before the order can reach a terminal state. The failed refund transaction will not retry automatically. The order process is stuck at the isWaitForFinancialCompletionRequired / waitForFinancialCompletion stage because the financial system never posts the WaitForFinancialComplete event.

Possible remediation:

TR260925-94249237, TR260925-94292417, TR260925-94546058, TR260925-94640512:
No action required. These orders are fully COMPLETED.

TR260925-94453037:
Confirm with the DIVA team whether this order has been fulfilled on their end. If DIVA confirms fulfillment and the shipment status was sent but not processed by Hybris, the consignment statuses need to be manually updated (READY to SHIPPED/COMPLETED) and the omnichannel-consignment-sub-process needs to be retriggered. This follows the remediation pattern from TKME-2028 where orders were manually pushed to COMPLETED after DIVA confirmed fulfillment. If DIVA has not yet fulfilled the order, this is an external dependency — the order will remain in ORDER_SPLIT until DIVA sends the shipment status.

TR260925-94514044:
The MasterPass REFUND_FOLLOW_ON transaction (450,000 TRY) is in ERROR status. The refund needs to be retried. This can be done by creating a new refund transaction entry or by resetting the failed transaction status and retriggering the refund flow via HAC script. The order process will remain in RUNNING state until the financial completion event is posted. Alternatively, if the refund cannot be retried, the order process can be manually advanced past the financial completion stage, but the refund failure should be resolved first to ensure the customer receives their money back.

For both stuck orders, no single reusable PC ticket covers this exact scenario. The closest existing reusable tickets are PC-44946 (TR Order Split — update external service status + retrigger consignment, manual, no script) and PC-52605 (generic process restart for stuck business processes, has script script-TKME-2279-retrigger-business-process.groovy). A new PC ticket may be needed if a HAC script is required for remediation.

solution.excerpt:
Ticket Summary: Update or create Cronjob for autocleanup
Generated: 2026-09-03T20:00:00Z

Hi Arvind ,

The SMI cluster database is experiencing recurring high storage issues because several Hybris snapshot tables and custom event log tables grow unboundedly without any automated retention cleanup. SAP has raised incident 002075129500011086542026 and advised running batched DELETE statements from HAC per KBA 3716653, but this is a manual workaround and needs to be automated as a scheduled cronjob.

The six target tables fall into two categories. First, snapshot tables generated by Hybris when snapshot persistence is enabled for standard types: users4sn (User, typecode 4), paymentinfos42sn (PaymentInfo, typecode 42), pricerows1055sn (PriceRow, typecode 1055), and addresses23sn (Address, typecode 23). These tables follow Hybris naming convention where the numeric suffix is the typecode and the sn suffix denotes snapshot. They accumulate every versioned snapshot for their respective types and have no built-in expiry mechanism. Second, the tasklogs table which is the standard Hybris process engine task log, accumulating process execution metadata. Third, the tokoeventlog table which is a custom type defined in tokocore-items.xml at line 38446 with deployment table TokoEventLog and typecode 11164. The TokoEventLog type stores event messages with a target item reference, a message string, and an infoMap, indexed by itemtype, target, and creationtime. Both tasklogs and tokoeventlog are write-heavy tables that grow continuously during normal operation.

No existing DB-level cleanup cronjob exists in the Toko codebase for these tables. The codebase has several domain-specific cleanup jobs (CachedServiceabilityCleanupJob, TokoOtpSessionCleanupJob, TokoSimContractDocumentCleanupJob, TokoBackofficeReportsCleanupJobPerformable, TokoTradeInDataCleanupJob, AltchaCleanupJob), but all operate through the Hybris model layer using FlexibleSearch and ModelService.remove, not through raw SQL DELETE statements. The SAP-requested queries use DELETE TOP(200000) with DATEADD-based retention filtering, which is a SQL Server batched-delete pattern that bypasses the model layer entirely. This is intentional for performance: deleting 200K rows at a time avoids lock escalation and transaction log bloat on large tables.

A PC ticket PC-53529 has already been created for this work, titled "[SAM-24720] Create DB cleanup cronjobs for SMI cluster" and is currently in To Do status. A previous similar ticket SAM-20914 ("Update or create Cronjob for autocleanup") was resolved as Closed, and HGE-8069 ("TokoEventLog Cleanup") is in Launch Verification status, indicating prior work has been done on TokoEventLog cleanup specifically. The ticket SAM-18467 ("Please check tasklog, tokoeventlog table size") was also completed, confirming these table sizes have been monitored before.

The recommended approach is to create a new JobPerformable class, TokoDbCleanupJobPerformable, in the tokocore extension that executes the six batched DELETE statements using direct JDBC (not FlexibleSearch) to match the SQL Server-specific syntax. The job should be configurable via project.properties for retention periods and batch sizes, scheduled via a CronJob instance with a Trigger in tokodeployment ImpEx, and configured to run during low-traffic windows. The existing PC-53529 should cover this implementation. The job should be created on all SMI cluster environments where snapshot persistence is enabled. No Kibana log analysis or HAC FlexiQuery was performed for this ticket as it is a database maintenance request, not an order-level issue.

Thanks,

Aryan

## Remediation

1. PC-53529 already exists for this work. Implement the TokoDbCleanupJobPerformable in tokocore with the six DELETE statements as specified.
2. Configure retention periods via project.properties: toko.db.cleanup.tasklogs.retention.months=2, toko.db.cleanup.users.retention.months=1, toko.db.cleanup.paymentinfo.retention.months=3, toko.db.cleanup.pricerows.retention.months=3, toko.db.cleanup.addresses.retention.months=3, toko.db.cleanup.tokoeventlog.retention.months=3
3. Create CronJob instance and Trigger via ImpEx in tokodeployment, scheduled to run daily during off-peak hours.
4. Deploy to SMI cluster environments. Verify table sizes decrease after first run.
5. Refer to HGE-8069 for prior TokoEventLog cleanup work and SAM-20914 for the previous autocleanup implementation pattern.

actions.comment:
Hi [~t.zaidi@samsung.com] ,

The order AE260901-08628165 has 2 SC+ subscriptions by design (AE AddedServiceConfig for SMC has maxPerOrder=3). Both subscriptions were created from the same Checkout.com token during order placement.

When a user updates card details from the my-orders page, the Checkout.com card update callback flows through TokoCheckoutDotComFacadeImpl.doAuthorize() -> handleSubscriptionOrder() -> updatePaymentInfo(). The updatePaymentInfo() method (line 995) calls getPaymentTransactionForOrderAndPid() which searches the order PaymentTransactions by paymentProvider and paymentId, returning the most recent matching PT. It then gets the subscriptionData from that PT and updates only that single subscription token, paymentInfo, and paymentMode.

All 4 PaymentTransactions on this order are linked to sub1 (ARE26I0411465355) or have no subscriptionData. Zero PTs exist for sub2 (ARE26I0461157598). When the card update callback fires, getPaymentTransactionForOrderAndPid() finds PT4 (created Sep 17, linked to sub1), updates sub1 token successfully, but sub2 is never reached.

The Adyen facade handles this correctly via updateEachSubscriptionData() (line 4523) which iterates all ExternalServiceEntries on the order and updates each subscription token + paymentInfo individually. Checkout.com had no equivalent iteration logic.

We also verified that the manual "_1" appended to the token is not a contributing factor. The token is an output that gets SET from the Checkout.com response source ID, not an input used for PT matching. The subscription ONHOLD status does not block the card update flow either -- the update code does not check subscription status.

Proposed fix: In TokoCheckoutDotComFacadeImpl.updatePaymentInfo(), after updating the matched PT subscription, iterate all remaining subscriptions on the order and call updateSingleSubscriptionPaymentInfo() for each, mirroring Adyen updateEachSubscriptionData() pattern. The existing updateSingleSubscriptionPaymentInfo() method handles the actual update logic per subscription (token, paymentInfo, paymentMode). This is the minimal change that addresses the bug.

Thanks,
Aryan
